newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen buying 104,000t soybeans, 88,000t corn.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen buying 104,000t soybeans, 88,000t corn.

text.p: Taiwanese buyers are expected to hold four tenders for a total of 104,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 88,000 tonnes of corn next week, traders said on Thursday.
State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp was seen tendering for a combined shipment of 18,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. soybeans, they said.
Taiwan Sugar's shipment is scheduled for delivery from the U.S. Gulf from October 25 to November 10.
Taiwan's Hui Shung group is also expected to place a tender for a combined shipment of 38,000-tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 16,000 tonnes U.S. corn.
The Hui Shung group's shipment would be scheduled for delivery from November 10 to 25 from the U.S. Gulf or November 26 to December 9 from the Pacific Northwest, they said.
The Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association Taichung group would also place a tender for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. soybeans, the traders added.
The shipment is likely to be scheduled for delivery from December 26 to January 9 from the Gulf of Mexico or January 10 to 24 from the Pacific Northwest.
Grain traders said that the FGEP corn buying group would return to the market for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. corn after a dispute over the tender price with seller Agrex.

A tender for the disputed shipment was placed on September 24 and FGEP buyers had said it was awarded to Agrex as the lowest bidder at 89 U.S. cents a tonne over the December Chicago corn futures contract.
But the supplier disputed the price and said the bid was 89.20 U.S. cents.
The two sides refused to enter into a final contract.
The disputed shipment would be slated for delivery from December 10-25 from the U.S. Gulf or December 26 to January 9 from the Pacific Northwest, traders said.
No retender date has been set, but traders said the group would try again early next week.
Local buyers said pressure from the approaching U.S. corn harvest season and the absence of significant weather concerns for the North American crop should keep corn prices low.

"Corn still looks bearish for the nearby harvest season and no serious frost is expected," an executive at Taiwan's Formosa Oilseeds said. Formosa Oilseeds is a key buyer in Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group.
Local buying sentiment remains bullish for soybean as Taiwanese firms believe delayed planting in the United States this year will lead to a smaller crop.
Domestic soymeal prices for Taipei delivery were quoted at between T$9.6 to T$9.8 a kg, unchanged from a week earlier.
Corn powder was priced at T$7.25 to T$7.30 a kg for Taipei delivery, up from T$7.20 to T$7.30 per kg last week.
U.S. Pacific Northwest to Taiwan freight rates were quoted at about US$10.00 a tonne and from the U.S. Gulf at around $20.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized November and December shipments.
In the domestic wheat market, traders said the Taiwan Flour Mills Association would not be a buyer in September as the group purchased a total of 98,000 tonnes U.S. wheat at a tender on August 29.
Association official Lu Wei-chih said Taiwan's wheat supplies should last until late October.
Wheat flour was quoted between T$14.55 to T$15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.
